label: Generating Functions
notes: Open by framing the chapter goal: a single scalar function can stand in for an entire symplectomorphism. Preview the three threads of generating functions, the symplectic action with orbits as critical points, and topological existence results for fixed points.

label: The Cotangent Bundle and Its Canonical Form
notes: Establish the cotangent bundle as the ambient phase space and pin down the tautological one-form and the canonical two-form. Stress that both are coordinate free and that the zero section is automatically a Lagrangian submanifold here.

label: Lagrangian Submanifolds as Graphs
notes: Recall that Lagrangians are half dimensional and isotropic. Emphasize the pullback identity showing a section is Lagrangian exactly when its defining one-form is closed, so locally that form is the differential of a generating scalar.

label: Generating Function of a Symplectomorphism
notes: Move to the twisted product where the graph of a symplectomorphism becomes Lagrangian. Explain how a favourable projection yields a generating function whose mixed partial derivatives reproduce both the old and the new momentum coordinates of the map.

label: Twist Maps and the Type-One Function
notes: Introduce the twist condition that makes old and new positions valid coordinates on the graph. The resulting first-kind generating function depends on both positions, and its partials recover the conjugate momenta with the expected opposite signs.

label: The Symplectic Action Functional
notes: Define the action of a path as the integral of p dq minus the Hamiltonian. Compute the first variation to show that stationary paths solve Hamilton's equations, so critical points of the action are precisely the orbits.

label: Discrete Hamiltonian Mechanics
notes: Discretize time so the action becomes a finite sum of step generating functions on a chain of positions. Stress that the broken trajectory model is genuinely finite dimensional, turning a variational problem into a gradient computation over nodes.

label: The Discrete Action Sum and Its Critical Points
notes: Derive the discrete Euler equation from setting the gradient to zero, a three-term recurrence matching momenta at junctions. Connect this to the notebook check that the gradient norm at marked critical corners stays below tolerance.

label: Hamilton-Jacobi Viewpoint
notes: Present the Hamilton-Jacobi equation as seeking a generating function that flattens the flow into constant new coordinates. Note it is the continuum limit of the discrete action picture and ties generating functions to integrable systems.

label: Generating Functions Quadratic at Infinity
notes: Explain why restricting to functions quadratic at infinity tames the behaviour outside a compact set. This makes critical points finite to count and sublevel topology computable, which is essential for global existence arguments with no explicit map formula.

label: Fixed Points and Lagrangian Intersections
notes: Identify fixed points of a symplectomorphism with intersections of its graph against the diagonal, equivalently critical points of a generating function. Morse theory then supplies an unavoidable lower bound on how many such points must exist.

label: Lagrangian Graphs over the Zero Section
notes: Close by tying the threads together: a projecting Lagrangian is the graph of a closed one-form whose zeros are critical points of its generating scalar. Topology of the base forces those intersections with the zero section.
